solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Coat with rich flounces in top half of trunk

indicators.note: to flounce is to move about in a showy, agitated way, so the letters of the fodder are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: A dress coat trimmed with lavish flounces covers the upper body of a mannequin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flounces' turns COAT and RICH into the answer; 'with' is a link. 'trunk' is the human torso, not a box or an elephant's nose.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes the chest cavity, the upper part of the torso between neck and abdomen.

clue.text: Always trouble, Henry discovered, getting crown off

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

indicators.note: the crown is the top of a down entry, so the word for discovered loses its first letter

parts.note: to have discovered something is to have found it

explanation.surface: A monarch is forever pestered when Henry is found to have lost his crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crown' is the top of a down entry, so the first letter goes; the royal surface about Henry is a decoy, with Henry the unit of inductance.
explanation.definitionFit: To pursue or harass someone relentlessly is to bother them constantly, never letting up.

clue.text: Heartless tennis pro smashed sharp return

indicators.note: broken into pieces, so the remaining letters are reassembled in a fresh order
the middle of the word tennis is cut out, its central pair of letters dropped

explanation.surface: A tennis professional, lacking spirit, smashes a ball back hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' takes NN from TENNIS, leaving TEIS; 'smashed' rearranges TEIS plus PRO.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick, cutting retort in conversation, or a fencer's counter-thrust, is a pointed reply.

clue.text: Slim Apple product that flips, perfect for selfie taker?

indicators.note: flipping turns the slim-plus-apple pairing end to end, so it is read backwards

parts.note: to pare is to trim or slim down
a Mac is a computer made by Apple
to hone a skill is to perfect it

explanation.surface: A thin new gadget from Apple with a folding design would be ideal for taking self-portraits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that flips' turns PARE + MAC into CAMERAP; HONE completes it. 'for' is a link; the flip-phone surface misdirects.
explanation.definitionFit: A mobile handset with a built-in lens is what people use to snap pictures of themselves.

clue.text: Conservative formerly a Liberal in disguise

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative, the British party
once means at some time in the past
L is the abbreviation for Liberal, a British party

explanation.surface: A politician who used to be a Liberal now hides inside the Conservative party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word between wordplay and definition, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To hide or mask something keeps it from view, just as a costume hides identity.

clue.text: Twin Peaks agent making arrest

parts.note: a cap is a peak or summit
a tor is a rocky hill peak, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: An FBI agent from the TV series Twin Peaks makes an arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twin Peaks' is the TV series in the surface but gives two words for peak side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: One who seizes and holds a prisoner is the person who has taken them into custody.

clue.text: Prudence reduced component of jam?

indicators.note: cut short, so the word for prudence loses its final letter

parts.note: care means caution or prudence

explanation.surface: A careful person called Prudence makes less of the preserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' drops the last letter of CARE. The jam is a traffic jam, not a preserve; the question mark flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: A traffic jam is made up of many motor vehicles queued on the road, each one part of it.

clue.text: Calendar easier to understand when one turns to November

indicators.note: one letter in the word changes into another, as the clue says it becomes November

parts.note: plainer means clearer, easier to understand
I is the Roman numeral for one
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A diary becomes easier to follow once the year reaches November.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when one turns to November' changes the I of PLAINER to N.
explanation.definitionFit: A diary or wall chart for organising appointments is a schedule laid out by date.

clue.text: Old underwear worn by queen had stretch

indicators.note: the undergarment is put on the queen, so it wraps around her letter

parts.note: a vest is a British undergarment worn under a shirt
R is for Regina, Latin for queen
ate means had, as in had a meal

explanation.surface: An old undergarment put on by the queen was a little too tight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worn by' puts R inside VEST to make VERST.
explanation.definitionFit: To exaggerate is to stretch the truth, claiming more than the facts allow.

clue.text: Useless parking which might activate airbag?

parts.note: bum is slang for worthless or useless, as in a bum deal
P stands for parking on road signs

explanation.surface: Poor parking that might set off a car's airbag.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is by example: a collision sets off an airbag.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor collision between vehicles is the kind of knock that could trigger a car's safety cushion.

clue.text: Maidens fearfully eager on vacation? I see what you mean

parts.note: M is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for a maiden over
in dread means fearfully

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so only the outside letters of eager are kept

explanation.surface: Young women nervously look forward to the holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' empties EAGER to ER. A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored. The definition is a telepathist's boast.
explanation.definitionFit: A telepathist claims to perceive another person's thoughts, seeing intentions without being told.

clue.text: Police officers request fewer dishes to eat in mess

parts.note: DIs are Detective Inspectors

indicators.note: the phrase for asking for fewer dishes takes in, or eats, the following small word

parts.note: at a restaurant you would order less

explanation.surface: Detectives ask for smaller portions when dining in the canteen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' looks like a military canteen, in keeping with the dining surface, but it means untidiness; ordering less is what a diner asking for fewer dishes does.
explanation.definitionFit: Untidiness or chaos is a state of disarray, the opposite of neatness.

clue.text: Invisible leaf rustler in Spooner's sunny meadows

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the starting sounds of words, so the initial sounds of the two words are exchanged

parts.note: bright means sunny
leas are meadows or grassland

explanation.surface: Something unseen stirs the foliage in bright fields.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the first sounds of BRIGHT LEAS gives the sound of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle wind cannot be seen yet stirs the foliage on trees.

clue.text: Covertly withdraw rent increase

parts.note: a rent is a tear or hole in fabric
to up a price is to increase it

explanation.surface: Someone quietly backs out of a rise in their rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like money paid to a landlord but is a tear.
explanation.definitionFit: To hide away somewhere, as fugitives do, is to retreat out of sight.

clue.text: Smelling Florence upset fanciful thespian

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the short name is read backwards

parts.note: Flo is a short form of the name Florence
an actory person is theatrical; actor plus y suggests a fancy, stagey performer

explanation.surface: Florence was disturbed by an actor with a vivid imagination who smelt odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns FLO to OLF. The blog reads ACTOR + Y as the fanciful thespian.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to the sense of smell, as in the nerves that detect odours.

clue.text: Funny bouncer burst on stage

indicators.note: one word is placed on, after, the other, a charade in answer order

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race
to break or burst out

explanation.surface: A comic doorman bursts onto the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket this is a spin delivery that bounces and turns unexpectedly, hence funny bouncer; the surface suggests a nightclub doorman. 'break a leg' is also stage slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin bowler's delivery that pitches and turns from leg to off behaves oddly after it bounces.

clue.text: Fresh food spoilt after spending days at sea

indicators.note: spoilt food has gone off, so the remaining letters are jumbled
spending something uses it up, so the abbreviation for days is taken out of the fodder

explanation.surface: Fresh provisions go bad after days on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after spending' removes D from FRESH FOOD; 'spoilt' rearranges FRESHFOO.
explanation.definitionFit: Located or operating away from the coast, out on the water, describes something on the open ocean.

clue.text: Employee following cuts worked faster

indicators.note: the abbreviation for following slices into the rearranged letters
worked as in worked over or kneaded, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: f is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A worker, after the budget cuts, works harder and quicker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' rearranges FASTER; 'cuts' puts F inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the staff of an organisation, especially a newspaper or office, is a worker there.

clue.text: Message typed in centre of Lincoln when cycling, "Totally lost"

indicators.note: cycling moves a letter round from the front of the assembled letters to the back

parts.note: a text is a message typed on a phone

indicators.note: the middle letter of the seven-letter word Lincoln

explanation.surface: Someone texts from the middle of Lincoln while out on a bike, saying they are completely lost.
explanation.walkthrough: TEXT + IN + C gives TEXTINC; 'when cycling' moves the first T to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A species that has died out completely is gone for good, never to return.

clue.text: Good mark on student's work barely gets pass

parts.note: a teacher puts a tick on correct work

indicators.note: bared means stripped, so the word gets loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: A small mark of approval on a pupil's essay is just enough to scrape through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barely' strips GETS to ET. 'pass' seems a verb but is a noun: a permit for entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A permit or slip granting entry or travel is a document allowing admission.

clue.text: Daring commenter's first on Times for The Times

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the other, so it comes first
only the opening letter of the word commenter's is taken

parts.note: the newspaper speaking of its own era would say our age

explanation.surface: A blog commenter is the first to remark on the Times crossword for the Times for The Times site.
explanation.walkthrough: Times for The Times is the blog that discusses this puzzle, so the surface is an in-joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravery or boldness in the face of danger is what lets someone dare to act.

clue.text: In fight lacking finesse, Esther narrowly avoids being knocked out

indicators.note: the book's name is placed in the middle of the two words for fight and coarse

parts.note: a scrap is a fight
rough means crude, lacking finesse
Esth is the standard abbreviation for the Book of Esther in the Bible

explanation.surface: Esther narrowly survives a crude brawl without being flattened.
explanation.walkthrough: Esther looks like a boxer's name in the surface; she is the Old Testament book, abbreviated as in Bible references.
explanation.definitionFit: To get through a contest by the narrowest margin is to survive elimination only just.

clue.text: Try to save oxygen pump keeping person alive

parts.note: a judge hears or tries a case

indicators.note: save means except, so the chemical symbol is removed from the little word

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Doctors attempt to conserve oxygen while a machine keeps a patient alive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'save' means except: TO without O leaves T. 'Try' is the legal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ that pumps blood through the body keeps a person living.

clue.text: Fan noticed ground's secret repository

indicators.note: ground as in crushed or milled, so the letters are broken down and reformed

explanation.surface: A fan was spotted on the sports ground at a hidden storage spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' rearranges FAN NOTICED; the 's is 'has', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A trusted friend to whom secrets are told keeps them stored away safely.

clue.text: Used to going up and down

indicators.note: in a down entry the word reads the same upwards as downwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Something that was once in the habit of rising and falling.
explanation.definitionFit: The past auxiliary of habit: 'she used to sing' and 'she did sing' both point to past action.

clue.text: Just out of frame, Indian prince pulled back

indicators.note: pulled back means drawn in reverse, so the title is read from right to left

parts.note: a raja is an Indian prince or king

explanation.surface: An Indian prince is drawn back, just outside the picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just out of frame' describes a door slightly open in its frame, not a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: A door slightly open stands a little away from its doorframe.

clue.text: Cross drunk heard wedding party finished early

indicators.note: heard means spoken aloud, so the slang word for drunk gives letters that sound like it

parts.note: high means intoxicated

indicators.note: cut short at the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: the bride is a party, one of the two people, at a wedding

explanation.surface: A tipsy guest overhears that the wedding reception ended early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' gives HY for the sound of HIGH; 'finished early' cuts the last E off BRIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross between two plants or animals is offspring bred from different kinds.

clue.text: When Dante's Peak was new to screens

indicators.note: to screen is to hide or enclose, so the little word surrounds the word for new

parts.note: recent means new

explanation.surface: The film Dante's Peak was new to cinema screens.
explanation.walkthrough: Dante's Peak is a 1997 disaster film, but here it means the poet Dante's heyday, the Italian 1300s.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian fourteenth century was the age in which the poet Dante flourished.
